Chapter 2: The Three Types of Performers—Good, Great, and Unstoppable
Let’s take a closer look at what it really means to be relentless. If you think about it, not everyone tackles challenges the same way. There’s actually a whole spectrum when it comes to performance.
On one end, you’ll find people who are perfectly content with being good. Then there are those who reach for greatness. And finally, there’s a rare group—those who are truly unstoppable.
So, how do you spot the difference?
Let’s start with the first level: the good performers. These are the folks you can always count on. They’re reliable, they follow directions, and they almost never make mistakes. They’re valuable team players, but you probably won’t see them stepping into the spotlight or taking big risks. For them, it’s all about meeting the standards that someone else has set, and they’re usually okay with just doing a good job.
Now, step up a notch to the great performers. These people aren’t just doing what’s expected—they’re pushing for more. They love a challenge, crave recognition, and they’re often driven by competition. You’ll see them taking the lead, and when things are going well, their motivation is sky-high. But here’s the thing—their drive can fade when things get tough, or when the rewards aren’t so obvious.
And then, at the very top, are the unstoppable ones—the Cleaners. These individuals are something special. They set their own standards and never settle, no matter what. Their motivation? It comes from within. They don’t get distracted by praise or criticism. When the pressure’s on, they stay calm. They’re not afraid to fail, and they’re always searching for new ways to get better.
If you break it down, it looks like this:
Good: Follows instructions, meets expectations, avoids mistakes.
Great: Goes beyond expectations, thrives on recognition, and is fueled by competition.
Unstoppable: Sets personal standards, is never satisfied, driven from within, and actually embraces discomfort.
Here’s something to pay attention to: the difference between these types isn’t just about talent or skill. It’s really about mindset, habits, and the willingness to do what others simply won’t.
For example, a good performer might stop practicing once they’ve got the basics down. A great performer keeps going until they’re the best on the team. But the unstoppable performer? They’ll keep pushing even after reaching the top, always looking for that next edge.
In real life, these differences show up in subtle ways. The good performer might shy away from risks because they don’t want to make mistakes. The great performer will take risks, but only when the reward is clear. The unstoppable performer? They take calculated risks simply because they’re focused on growth, not just on winning.
Now, this framework isn’t about judging or labeling anyone. It’s really about helping you figure out where you are right now, and what it takes to move up to the next level. The journey from good, to great, to unstoppable isn’t about completely changing who you are. It’s about adopting new habits and shifting how you think.
So, how do you start moving up this spectrum? There are a few practical things you can do:
First—take initiative. Don’t just wait for someone to tell you what to do. Look for ways to add value, to solve problems before anyone else even notices them.
Second—seek feedback. Don’t dodge criticism. Treat it like a tool for growth instead of a blow to your self-esteem.
Third—embrace failure. Think of your mistakes as stepping stones, not setbacks. Every misstep is a chance to learn and get better.
And finally—stay focused. Distractions are everywhere, but the people who become unstoppable are the ones who stick to their long-term goals, even when progress feels slow.
The path to becoming unstoppable isn’t easy. It means being honest with yourself about both your strengths and your weaknesses. It means staying committed to improving, even when you’ve already tasted success.
So here’s the key takeaway: If you want to be more than just good, or even great—if you want to be truly unstoppable—you’ve got to keep searching for the next challenge, and never stop looking for ways to grow.
